items.summary:
CRO recommends containment-only execution. Active delivery is full at 10/10 slots, with 63 overflow items, 42 improvements awaiting measurement, 17 failed implementation requests, and unavailable operations/security evidence. Do not create proposals, change requests, experiments, telemetry, deployments, spend, dependencies, or requeues this cycle.

Retain these deferred, reversible opportunities for CEO/CTO review after gates clear:
1) Affiliate-path clarity on allthingsmasonic.com: evidence includes 61 Amazon clicks and 0 site-attributed orders or commission for the available window; prototype one existing commercial-page CTA/disclosure arrangement. Metric: affiliate click-through and attributed orders, with revenue remaining unknown until attribution resolves. Learn in 14 days or 100 relevant impressions/clicks. Risks: attribution is partial and the site already has active work; MIT/shadcn-style UI components are optional inspiration only and require dependency/security review.
2) Search-intent content module using microsoft/markitdown: convert one rights-cleared source document into a reviewed Markdown draft for an existing SEO page. Evidence: MIT license, 8/8 bounded lab checks passed, and 22 purpose-specific keyword hits. Metric: indexed impressions, CTR, and qualified sessions versus the existing page. Smallest prototype is an offline conversion of one fixture with human review; no production dependency or automated publishing. Risks: source rights, parsing accuracy, prompt/content quality, maintenance, and dependency provenance.
3) Accessible comparison/diagram block using mermaid-js/mermaid or shadcn-ui/ui: prototype one static, locally rendered component for a high-intent page after current measurement windows clear. Evidence: MIT licenses and supported CRO-lab fit; Mermaid had no safe native checks without dependency installation, while shadcn/ui passed 3/3 bounded checks. Metric: CTA engagement or affiliate-path continuation, measured with existing telemetry only. Risks: bundle weight, accessibility, dependency maintenance, and no demonstrated causal lift.

These remain backlog hypotheses, not approvals. Each requires owner-approved implementation, CTO/security review, license and dependency validation, a preview, deterministic tests, rollback, and an existing-telemetry measurement plan. Financial outcomes, ROI, and causal lift remain unknown; provider aggregate commission remains unattributed.
